S4.01.note: Code shows /new handler only; the exact empty-screen layout was not read.
steps: Run agi in a terminal and sign in.
Look at the first screen: it should show the input box ready to type in.
Type /new and press Enter.
Check the screen is a fresh empty conversation with a ready input box, compared with Expected.
S4.01.where: agi (opens the app after sign-in), then type /new

S4.02.needs: a signed-in account with at least one past conversation
S4.02.note: Transcript display on open was not confirmed in the code read.
steps: In the app, type /resume and press Enter.
In the session list that opens, move to a past conversation and press Enter.
Check that its earlier messages are shown.
Type a new message and send it to confirm the conversation continues.
S4.02.where: agi, then type /resume (or /sessions) and press Enter

S4.03.needs: a signed-in account with past conversations
S4.03.note: The in-app /search command is a web search, not conversation search.
steps: In a terminal run agi --search "<a word from an old chat>".
Check that past conversations with that word in their title or messages are listed.
Optionally, in the app type /sessions search <a word> and press Enter.
Open one result and compare with Expected.
S4.03.where: agi --search "<keyword>" (from a terminal), or in the app type /sessions search <keyword>

S4.04.needs: a signed-in account with an archived conversation
S4.04.note: Archiving itself is done with the session archive subcommand; no in-app archived list was found.
steps: Run agi session list --archived in a terminal.
Check that archived conversations are listed.
Run agi session unarchive <id> with an id from the list, then run agi session list to confirm it left the archived list.
Run agi session delete <id> and read the confirmation prompt before answering.
S4.04.where: agi session list --archived (terminal); restore with agi session unarchive <id>; delete with agi session delete <id>

labels.text: Browse and create the projects in your AGI account.

steps: Run agi projects list.
Check that the account's projects are listed.
Run agi projects create "Test project" and then run agi projects list again.
Check the new project appears.
S4.06.where: agi projects list (terminal); create with agi projects create <name>

labels.text: Show one project: description, instructions, knowledge files and conversation count.

S4.07.needs: a signed-in account with a project
S4.07.note: The output is text; no links to chats or files were found in the code read.
steps: Run agi projects list and pick a project name.
Run agi projects show "<project name>".
Check the output shows the name, description, instructions, knowledge files and conversation count.
Note whether it offers links to the project's chats and files, compared with Expected.
S4.07.where: agi projects show <project name or id> (terminal)

labels.text: Rename a project or change its description or instructions.

S4.10.needs: a signed-in account with a project
S4.10.note: Whether the instructions then apply to chats in that project was not checked in the UI.
steps: Run agi projects show "<project name>" and note the current instructions.
Run agi projects edit "<project name>" --instructions "Answer in short bullet points".
Run agi projects show "<project name>" again.
Check the new instructions are shown, compared with Expected.
S4.10.where: agi projects edit <project name or id> --instructions "<text>" (terminal); view with agi projects show <project>

labels.text: Keep it with the account project this directory is linked to

S4.12.needs: a signed-in account with a project
S4.12.note: Only the add scope flag was found; no project-only memory view or scope control was found in the code read.
steps: Link a folder to a project with agi projects link "<project name>" from that folder.
Run agi memory add --project "Test memory for this project".
Run agi memory list.
Check whether the project memory is shown separately from account memory, compared with Expected.
S4.12.where: agi memory add --project "<text>" (terminal); list account memories with agi memory list

labels.text: Manage the account's scheduled agent tasks in AGI cloud.

S4.17.note: Exact flag names were not all read; use each subcommand's --help.
steps: Run agi schedules list and read the status and cadence columns.
Run agi schedules create with a name, a cron expression such as "0 9 * * *", and a prompt (see agi schedules create --help for flags).
Run agi schedules pause <name>, then agi schedules resume <name>.
Run agi schedules run <name>, then agi schedules delete <name> and read the prompt before confirming.
Compare each step with Expected.
S4.17.where: agi schedules list (terminal); create with agi schedules create, change with agi schedules edit, pause/resume/run/delete with the matching subcommands

S4.18.needs: a signed-in account with a schedule that has run
S4.18.note: No separate show command for a schedule's configuration was found; it may only appear in the list output (not verified).
steps: Run agi schedules list to get a schedule id or name.
Run agi schedules runs "<name>".
Check the run history is listed.
Check that the schedule's prompt, cadence and next run are visible, compared with Expected.

S4.19.needs: a signed-in account and a GitHub checkout
steps: Run agi code list in a terminal.
Check the cloud coding sessions are listed.
Inside a GitHub checkout, run agi code start "Add a README line" and answer the review prompt.
Run agi code list again and check the new session appears.
S4.19.where: agi code list (terminal); start one with agi code start "<task>" inside a GitHub checkout

labels.text: Show one cloud Code session: where it works and what each turn did.

S4.20.needs: a signed-in account with a cloud Code session
S4.20.note: No diff view or steering composer was found in the CLI code read; agi code show is the only workspace command found.
steps: Run agi code list and copy a session id.
Run agi code show <session id>.
Check the transcript of each turn is shown.
Look for file changes or diffs and a box to send the next instruction; compare with Expected.
S4.20.where: agi code show <session id> (terminal); open in browser with agi code open <session id>

S4.23.needs: a signed-in account with library items
S4.23.note: The Library command covers images, videos and files; artifacts are listed under agi artifacts.
steps: Run agi library.
Check the list shows generated and uploaded images, videos and files.
Run agi library --kind image and check only images are listed.
Run agi library show <id> or agi library download <id> for one item and check it opens or saves.
S4.23.where: agi library (terminal); filter with agi library --kind image and agi library --search <text>

labels.text: Browse, read and publish the artifacts in your AGI account.

steps: Run agi artifacts list.
Check the artifacts are listed newest first.
Run agi artifacts show <id> to print one, or agi artifacts open <id> to open it in the browser.
Compare with Expected.
S4.25.where: agi artifacts list (terminal); also the in-app /artifacts

labels.text: /image <prompt> draws an image on your account and saves it here

S4.27.needs: a signed-in paid or allowed account
S4.27.note: No separate studio screen was found; image generation is a command inside the chat.
steps: In the app, type /image --aspect 16:9 a red bicycle on a beach and press Enter.
Watch for the generated image to appear, and press Esc to stop if needed.
Type /image last to see the settings the last image used.
Run agi library and check the image is in the account library.
S4.27.where: In the app, type /image <prompt> (flags such as --aspect 16:9 come before the prompt); also agi image "<prompt>" in a terminal

S4.33.note: These are local agent definition files, not account-hosted custom assistants; there is no in-app edit screen, only /agents set and /agents rename.
steps: In the app, type /agents and press Enter to list agents.
Type /agents new my-helper and check a new agent is created.
Type /agents show my-helper to view it.
Type /agents delete my-helper --yes and check it is removed.
S4.33.where: In the app, type /agents (then /agents show <name>, /agents new <name>, /agents delete <name> --yes)

labels.text: Usage: /skills import <path to SKILL.md or its folder>

S4.35.needs: a folder with a SKILL.md file to import
S4.35.note: Remove behaviour and the available-skills catalogue were not read in full.
steps: In the app, type /skills and press Enter to list installed skills.
Type /skills-toggle and turn one skill off, then back on.
Type /skills import <path to a SKILL.md folder> to install one.
Type /skills remove <name> to remove a skill and compare the list with Expected.
S4.35.where: In the app, type /skills (list), /skills import <path>, /skills-toggle; author with /create-skill

steps: In the app, type /plugins and press Enter.
Look at the installed and available tabs.
In a terminal run agi marketplace browse, then agi plugin list.
Use agi plugin disable <name> and agi plugin enable <name> and check the list changes.
S4.36.where: In the app, type /plugins; also agi plugin list and agi marketplace browse in a terminal

S4.38.note: Context and price columns were not confirmed in the list output.
steps: In the app, type /models and press Enter to see the model list with its flags.
Type /model and choose a model from the picker.
In a terminal run agi models list.
Run agi models set <model name> and check the default changes.
S4.38.where: In the app, type /models (list) or /model (picker); in a terminal run agi models list and agi models set <model>

labels.text: Show the account's managed allowance from the shared usage ledger.

S4.39.note: Per-window (session, weekly, credits) limits and reset times and recent history were not confirmed in the code read.
steps: In the app, type /usage and press Enter.
Check the token totals, cost and per-model breakdown.
In a terminal run agi usage.
Check the account allowance against the plan limits and reset times, compared with Expected.
S4.39.where: In the app, type /usage; in a terminal run agi usage and agi plans

S4.41.note: No notifications settings screen was found in the code read.
steps: In the app, type /personalize and answer the prompts such as What to call you.
Type /config show and check the saved values.
Type /memories and check the auto-memory setting can be changed.
Restart the app and check the values are kept.

S4.44.needs: a signed-in account and network access
S4.44.note: No help, docs or status links were found in the help or feedback code read.
steps: In the app, type /help and press Enter to see the command list.
Type /feedback I would like a dark theme and press Enter.
Check the app confirms the feedback was sent.
Compare the help output with Expected for links to docs and status.
S4.44.where: In the app, type /help; to send feedback type /feedback <text> or /bug <text>
